::: {.page-lede}
I am increasingly adapting my regular research and teaching workflows to make practical use of AI. I work with many AI agents and use many major model providers. My favorite is [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent), which I use to build reusable workflows that support research planning, coding, analysis, writing, course development, and classroom activities. These systems help me move between ideas and working tools more efficiently, while I remain responsible for the scientific questions, evidence, and decisions. I strongly support open-source development and aim to make these tools and workflows available for others to inspect, adapt, and build upon.

I wrote the opinion paper [When Statisticians Can Also Be AI Engineers, What Could We Build?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32105) to share some thoughts on how statisticians can build useful agentic tools. I advocate for a "domain-specific interactive harness" in which statistical expertise shapes the system's proactive behavior across multiple rounds of inquiry and interaction, especially in a data analytic task.

<article class="ai-project" aria-labelledby="proof-graphify-title">
<div class="ai-project-kind">Research reading</div>
<details class="ai-project-details">
<summary class="ai-project-summary">
<h3 id="proof-graphify-title" class="ai-project-title">Proof Graphify <a class="ai-project-version" href="https://github.com/rqzhu-aide/proof-graphify/tree/v3.3.5" aria-label="Version 3.3.5 on GitHub">v3.3.5</a><span class="ai-project-teaser">Graph style visualization of a proof and its dependencies.</span></h3>
</summary>
<div class="ai-project-content">
<p>Inspired by the <a href="https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify">Archify skill</a>, <a href="https://github.com/rqzhu-aide/proof-graphify">proof-graphify</a> turns TeX or PDF papers into interactive maps of main results, proof ideas, and important prerequisites. Readers can inspect source passages, follow dependencies, and share each map as a standalone HTML file. It shares the same backend core and interactive reader with <a href="https://github.com/rqzhu-aide/proof-graphify/tree/main/stat-proof-check">Proof Check</a>, a separate skill that examines written arguments using LLMs and independent review. Graphify supports reading and navigation; Proof Check records findings and unresolved limits. Neither provides formal proof verification. The toy example below illustrates the representer theorem.</p>

<article class="ai-project" aria-labelledby="causal-consultant-title">
<div class="ai-project-kind">Research workflow</div>
<details class="ai-project-details">
<summary class="ai-project-summary">
<h3 id="causal-consultant-title" class="ai-project-title">Interactive causal consulting <a class="ai-project-version" href="https://github.com/rqzhu-aide/causal-consultant/blob/main/README.md" aria-label="Version 8.0.15 on GitHub">v8.0.15</a><span class="ai-project-teaser">A conversational skill for developing causal questions, planning studies, and interpreting evidence.</span></h3>
</summary>
<div class="ai-project-content">
<p>The <a href="https://github.com/rqzhu-aide/causal-consultant">causal-consultant</a> skill helps researchers, students, and collaborators develop causal questions, plan studies and analyses, and interpret evidence through conversation. It seeks context that could change a recommendation, compares defensible approaches and alternative explanations, and keeps assumptions and uncertainty beside causal claims. Users can provide partial answers, ask for explanations, and choose useful next steps. Saved project memory retains decisions, findings, and unresolved questions across sessions; users can change direction or pause, and reports are optional. The companion <a href="https://github.com/rqzhu-aide/interactive-test">interactive-test</a> skill uses adaptive conversations with simulated users and separate review to examine scientific reasoning, useful recommendations, and continuity.</p>

<article class="ai-project" aria-labelledby="popping-title">
<div class="ai-project-kind">Teaching platform</div>
<details class="ai-project-details">
<summary class="ai-project-summary">
<h3 id="popping-title" class="ai-project-title">Popping <a class="ai-project-version" href="https://github.com/rqzhu-aide/popping/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md" aria-label="Version 1.3.3 on GitHub">v1.3.3</a><span class="ai-project-teaser">An interactive classroom platform for team discussions, presentations, and peer feedback.</span></h3>
</summary>
<div class="ai-project-content">
<p>Popping is an interactive classroom platform for instructors and students who use team-based discussion and presentation activities. Its Present and Challenge mode is a central feature: instructors can run timed team presentations and structured challenges, while students ask questions, respond to challenges, and submit peer ratings in real time. The platform also supports team selection, small-group discussion, peer recognition, and exportable participation and rating data. I currently deploy the Popping website on Render. Running a live instance requires a backend server and database to manage classroom sessions, teams, participation records, and ratings. Anyone can explore the classroom workflow through the private demo without creating an account.</p>

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  if (!window.lightboxQuarto) return;
  let imageLink = null;
  document.querySelectorAll(".ai-project-gallery a.lightbox").forEach(function (link) {
    link.addEventListener("click", function () {
      imageLink = link;
    }, true);
  });
  window.lightboxQuarto.on("open", function () {
    const dialog = document.getElementById("glightbox-body");
    if (!dialog) return;
    dialog.setAttribute("aria-label", "Project image viewer");
    dialog.setAttribute("aria-modal", "true");
    const closeButton = dialog.querySelector(".gclose");
    // Keep GLightbox's keyboard navigation in sync with the initial focus.
    closeButton.classList.add("focused");
    closeButton.focus({ preventScroll: true });
  });
  window.lightboxQuarto.on("close", function () {
    if (imageLink && imageLink.isConnected) {
      imageLink.focus({ preventScroll: true });
    }
    imageLink = null;
  });
});
</script>
